question:
For a real number $x$, let
\[
f(x)=\int_{-20}^{20}g(t)g(x-t)\,dt,
\]
where
\[
g(x)=\begin{cases}1,&x\in[0,1],\\0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Then $f(x)$ is equal to
solution:
If $x<0$ or $x>2$, the integral is zero. For $0\le x\le1$,
\[
f(x)=\int_{x-1}^{x}g(t)\,dt=x.
\]
For $1\le x\le2$,
\[
f(x)=\int_{x-1}^{x}g(t)\,dt=2-x.
\]
Thus option (A) is correct.
